model: S-Quad legacy sensor / sounder / strobe family
identification_notes: The 2013 range illustration shows a white S-Quad with a strobe lens. Several sensing and sounder variants share the body; read the complete part code on the label.
applicability_limits: Applies to the listed codes in 4188-779 Issue 10 (December 2013). This legacy strobe range is not an EN54-23 VAD reference. Later -VAD, -S and S4T Self-Test variants need their own documentation.
image_credit: Honeywell Gent range manual illustration

identification_notes: White circular mounting base with a large centre opening and screw terminals. The S4-700 marking is visible in the manufacturer picture.
applicability_limits: This is the standard S4-700 base. Check the complete code; 34000 adapter bases and coloured or specialist variants are outside this card. The detector head is a separate item.
image_credit: Honeywell Gent product image

identification_notes: Red square S4 call point with a white operating window, shown without a protective cover. The label and operating element identify the glass or resettable version.
applicability_limits: Covers S4-34800 (glass), S4-34805 (resettable) and their covered 34842/34845 variants. The housing does not establish the element fitted. EP weatherproof and keyswitch variants need separate instructions.
image_credit: Honeywell Gent range manual illustration

identification_notes: Light-coloured interface module with plug-in green terminals. The photograph shows the module itself, without its optional installation enclosure.
applicability_limits: Low-voltage S4-34450 only. Confirm the code before using a channel diagram; single-input, mains-switching and powered interfaces are different products. The linked 2015 panel document confirms the model and its function.
image_credit: Honeywell Gent product image

identification_notes: Red S-Cubed wall sounder with a rounded front. Check S3-V-R on the label: the front shape alone does not distinguish speech from tone-only models.
applicability_limits: The S3-V-R red voice sounder is listed in the 2015 S-Cubed Mark 3 table. This card does not identify a VAD, weatherproof EP or older VP variant by appearance. Check the installed system and firmware.
image_credit: Honeywell Gent product image

identification_notes: White round head with an enclosed centre and radial smoke-entry slots. The photograph shows a mounting base and address-card tab; confirm 55000-620APO on the detector label.
applicability_limits: The XP95 range also includes 55000-600 and black 55000-660 variants. Linked documents include the dedicated detector datasheet and a separate mounting-base guide. Confirm the head label, base and control-panel support.
image_credit: Apollo Fire Detectors product image

identification_notes: White round head with an open thermistor cage and a yellow central marker in this manufacturer photograph. Check the label for 55000-420APO and the A2S classification.
applicability_limits: This card covers the A2S 55000-420APO, not the CS 55000-401 or intrinsically safe variants. The dedicated detector datasheet distinguishes heat classifications; the separate archive guide covers mounting bases.
image_credit: Apollo Fire Detectors product image

identification_notes: White optical head with a solid central disc and slotted surround, shown on a mounting base. Its appearance is similar to XP95; the 58000-600APO label identifies this model.
applicability_limits: The archived datasheet is PP2606/2021 Issue 2; the manufacturer link is PP2606/2026 Issue 4. Response modes and supported features depend on the control panel; a similar housing does not establish protocol or edition.
image_credit: Apollo Fire Detectors product image

identification_notes: Low white head with a dark smoke-entry band and an exposed central heat-sensing cage. Confirm SA5100-710APO; the installation guide also describes different 720 and 810 variants.
applicability_limits: The product page and installation guide specify Discovery/CoreProtocol. The 2026 datasheet also lists XP95 in one table but not its technical-data field, so XP95 support is unconfirmed here. Check exact panel and firmware support.
image_credit: Apollo Fire Detectors product image

identification_notes: White low-profile detector with a rounded central cap and curved smoke-entry openings. Confirm ORB-OP-12001-APO on the head; the pictured base is a separate component.
applicability_limits: This is the standard optical model, not the ORB-OP-12003 flashing-LED, marine or I.S. variants. The linked installation guide covers the Orbis detector-head family; the manufacturer datasheet identifies the exact model.
image_credit: Apollo Fire Detectors product image

identification_notes: White round smoke head with an enclosed centre and angular smoke-entry slots. Confirm 55000-317APO on the label; Apollo uses similar housings across several detector types.
applicability_limits: This card covers the standard 55000-317 optical head. The 316 flashing-LED and 315 magnetic-test variants have separate part numbers. The dedicated manufacturer datasheet is linked; confirm the head, base and control-panel compatibility.
image_credit: Apollo Fire Detectors product image

identification_notes: Red square call point with an Apollo-branded resettable element and a round lower front fixing. Check SA5900-908APO; its face resembles the wireless XPander version.
applicability_limits: The 908 is the red wired indoor model. The linked guide also includes coloured and marine variants; their approvals and enclosure details differ. Match the part code and panel protocol before using a procedure.
image_credit: Apollo Fire Detectors product image

identification_notes: Red Apollo-style call point with XPander branding, shown with its resettable element operated. Confirm XPA-MC-14101-APO; a similar front is used on the wired Intelligent MCP.
applicability_limits: Wireless XPander device for an appropriate XPander system and interface, not a directly wired loop call point or a REACH device. The linked MK290 guide covers this exact indoor model; older XPA-MC-14006 has different documentation.
image_credit: Apollo Fire Detectors product image

model: Intelligent Open-Area Sounder VID (Red / White Flash)
identification_notes: Red open-area sounder with a small clear visual-indicator lens beside the sounder cone. Confirm SA5500-350APO on the label; flash colour cannot be established from an unlit picture.
applicability_limits: This is the white-flash VID model; EN 54-23 VAD coverage is not established by these documents. SA5500-351 uses red flash and SA5501 models have white housings. Tones, volumes and control functions depend on panel support.
image_credit: Apollo Fire Detectors product image

identification_notes: White rectangular surface enclosure labelled Intelligent Input/Output Unit, with front status positions. Confirm SA4700-102APO; other interface functions can share similar enclosures.
applicability_limits: The current datasheet lists XP95 and CoreProtocol operation, with Discovery using XP95 behaviour. Input modes and features vary with protocol and panel support. The enclosure photograph cannot identify the connected circuit or its function.
image_credit: Apollo Fire Detectors product image

identification_notes: White circular detector mounting base with metal contact groups and a removable XPERT address-card tab. Check the moulding or label for 45681-210APO.
applicability_limits: A base is not a detector. Similar Apollo bases have different electrical functions. The linked document covers XP95/Discovery mounting bases; verify the installed base and detector combination against their exact documentation.
image_credit: Apollo Fire Detectors product image

protocol: Mounting base for Soteria / Discovery / XP95
identification_notes: White circular mounting base with a wide cable opening, terminal ring and eight-position XPERT card. Confirm SA5000-200APO; red and black bases have separate part numbers.
applicability_limits: This card covers the white SA5000-200 base, not a complete detector or sounder. Physical fit alone does not confirm enabled functions; check the chosen head, addressing method and control-panel support.
image_credit: Apollo Fire Detectors product image

protocol: Apollo XP95 loop to REACH Wireless
identification_notes: White REACH interface enclosure with lower status indicators. Its display and navigation controls are inside the cover.
applicability_limits: REACH interface, not XPander. Linked PP5099 is revision 1 for firmware 1.0.3; match the actual firmware before following menu instructions.
image_credit: Apollo official product image from the linked manufacturer page.

protocol: Remote LED indicator; no separate addressable protocol
identification_notes: Small round white remote indicator with a central red LED behind the fire symbol. This is an indicator, not a detector.
applicability_limits: The MiniDisc indicates a connected detector’s status. Applicable terminals and electrical limits depend on the connected device and the MiniDisc instructions.
image_credit: Apollo official product image from the linked manufacturer page.

identification_notes: Manufacturer picture shows the beam head, separate controller and reflector together. Identify the SA7100-100APO set on its label.
applicability_limits: Auto-aligning intelligent model, not an assumed match for other Apollo beam products. The controller/head/reflector arrangement and permitted setup come from its own user guide.
image_credit: Apollo official product image from the linked manufacturer page.

identification_notes: White base-mounted flame detector with a dark circular sensing window. Three infrared sensing channels sit behind that window.
applicability_limits: Base-mounted IR3 version. The linked PP2331 Issue 9 expressly excludes the 45681-321 isolator base. Confirm the code and approved base; UV/IR2 and other housings are different products.
image_credit: Apollo official product image from the linked manufacturer page.

protocol: Apollo XP95/Discovery loop to XPander Wireless
identification_notes: Cream XPander enclosure with front power, fault and wireless-activity indicators. Check the full interface code.
applicability_limits: XPander device family only; Apollo states it is not CoreProtocol compatible. It is distinct from the REACH wireless interface and requires supported panel configuration.
image_credit: Apollo official product image from the linked manufacturer page.

identification_notes: White TimeSaver base with grouped screw terminals, shown without a head. The diode model shares the standard base’s exterior.
applicability_limits: Diode variant for the specified active end-of-line head-removal monitoring arrangement. Confirm the base label and system design; photo and shared wiring guide do not identify every TimeSaver variant.
image_credit: Apollo official product image from the linked manufacturer page.

identification_notes: White round detector with a red ring in the manufacturer datasheet. Read the underside code to distinguish it from similar CAST and ActiV heads.
applicability_limits: CA402 uses the CAST protocol. Confirm the CAST version of the panel and the correct base. Ring colour is a visual clue; it does not identify configuration or prove compatibility on its own. Linked manufacturer datasheet: DFU4020000 Rev 7, 05/08/21.
image_credit: C-TEC manufacturer datasheet image, via Acorn Fire & Security

identification_notes: White round detector with a blue ring in the manufacturer datasheet. Read the underside code to distinguish it from similar CAST and ActiV heads.
applicability_limits: CA414 uses the CAST protocol. Confirm the CAST version of the panel and the correct base. Ring colour is a visual clue; it does not identify configuration or prove compatibility on its own. Linked manufacturer datasheet: DFU4140000 Rev 7, 05/08/21.
image_credit: C-TEC manufacturer datasheet image, via Acorn Fire & Security

identification_notes: White round detector with a grey ring in the manufacturer datasheet. Read the underside code to distinguish it from similar CAST and ActiV heads.
applicability_limits: CA416 uses the CAST protocol. Confirm the CAST version of the panel and the correct base. Ring colour is a visual clue; it does not identify configuration or prove compatibility on its own. Linked manufacturer datasheet: DFU4160000 Rev 8, 05/08/21.
image_credit: C-TEC manufacturer datasheet image, via Acorn Fire & Security

identification_notes: Seven-terminal circular base, shown in the manufacturer wiring leaflet. This drawing shows the base without a detector head.
applicability_limits: CA408 standard base only. A similar circular base or relay-base variant can require different wiring; check the moulded code and the matching leaflet.
image_credit: C-TEC manufacturer illustration, via C-TEC Technical

model: CA470 CAST red manual call point
identification_notes: Red call point with an inward-arrow operating window and fire symbol. The manufacturer picture shows the standard surface-style housing.
applicability_limits: CA470 is the red CAST model with a resettable element. Check the code: other colours, conventional models and the CA47067 weatherproof enclosure have different scope.
image_credit: C-TEC manufacturer datasheet image, via Acorn Fire & Security

identification_notes: Rectangular grey CAST faceplate with Active, Polling and Input Fault indicators. Check CA730 on the module label.
applicability_limits: CA730 low-voltage I/O module only; CA731 mains-switching and other interfaces are separate models. The installation sheet provides the applicable monitored-input, relay and enclosure requirements.
image_credit: C-TEC manufacturer datasheet image, via Acorn Fire & Security

identification_notes: Clear-bodied base device with a directional optical lens, shown without a detector head or a finishing cap. Read the CA459A/W code on the device.
applicability_limits: This is a visual alarm device without a sounder. It is the corridor O-Class version; orientation matters. Do not substitute CA432A/W sounder/VAD or C-Class models from appearance alone. The linked DFU4315010 Rev 15 leaflet also covers sounder variants; use the CA459A/W row.
image_credit: C-TEC manufacturer datasheet image, via Acorn Fire & Security

model: Capture P15 / Q20 / D20 wired wall detectors
protocol: Wired 9–15 V DC; alarm/tamper outputs with EOL options. P15 and Q20 are PIR; D20 combines PIR and microwave.
identification_notes: Official shared Capture wall housing, with the circular lens and separate outer fascia.
applicability_limits: The shared cover does not identify P15, Q20 or D20. Confirm the product label and PCB before using the matching mode, wiring or coverage instructions. This card excludes -W radio, A20 Grade 3, PET and curtain versions.
image_credit: Texecom — official product image

model: Capture P15-W / Q20-W / D20-W wireless wall detectors
protocol: Texecom Ricochet two-way wireless; the listed -1000 radio types use 868.2–868.4 MHz. D20-W adds microwave sensing.
identification_notes: Official wireless wall-family picture; the Ricochet badge is part of the manufacturer artwork.
applicability_limits: Confirm the exact -W model and radio type. Similar 866 MHz and 433 MHz variants exist and are not interchangeable with the listed 868 MHz types. Ceiling, PET, LR50-W and C15-W variants have different coverage and are outside this card.
image_credit: Texecom — official product image

model: Capture CQ / CD wired ceiling detectors
protocol: Wired 9–15 V DC with alarm/tamper/EOL connections; CQ is quad PIR and CD is dual technology.
identification_notes: Round ceiling housing with central lens; manufacturer picture represents the common CQ/CD enclosure.
applicability_limits: Read the label to distinguish CQ from CD. This card covers the wired Grade 2 ceiling family, excluding CQ-W, CD-W and Grade 3 CA. Select coverage and mounting instructions for the actual model.
image_credit: Texecom — official product image

model: Impaq SC wired shock detector and magnetic contact
protocol: Wired powered shock/contact detector with alarm/tamper outputs and selectable EOL wiring.
identification_notes: Manufacturer photograph of the white SC unit with its separate magnetic-contact magnet.
applicability_limits: SC combines shock and opening detection. It is distinct from shock-only Impaq S, Impaq S Grade 3 and wireless SC-W, even though the linked family manual covers several of them.
image_credit: Texecom — official product image

model: Impaq SC-W wireless shock detector and magnetic contact
protocol: Texecom Ricochet two-way wireless, 868.2–868.4 MHz for GJAA1000; shock, magnetic contact and additional wired inputs.
identification_notes: White SC-W housing and separate magnet, shown in the manufacturer product photograph.
applicability_limits: Confirm SC-W and the GJAA radio type. Other frequency variants are listed in the manual. The wired SC and earlier Impaq models use different wiring and learning instructions.
image_credit: Texecom — official product image

protocol: Texecom Ricochet two-way wireless; GHAA1000 uses 868.2–868.4 MHz.
identification_notes: Official black-finish Micro Contact-W picture, showing the slim detector and separate magnet as one family.
applicability_limits: Finish alone does not identify the radio type. Confirm the model and region label; the manual also lists a different 866 MHz type. Do not confuse this opening detector with Micro Shock-W. The pictured colour is not a separate device family.
image_credit: Texecom — official product image

protocol: Texecom Ricochet two-way wireless; GHCA1000 uses 868.2–868.4 MHz.
identification_notes: Official black-finish Micro Shock-W picture; the single narrow body is a shock detector.
applicability_limits: This is the shock model, not a magnetic opening contact. Confirm GHCA radio type and installation edition. The 866 MHz type, deep-base accessory and alternate finishes do not establish the same regional approval or installation conditions.
image_credit: Texecom — official product image

protocol: Wired 9–16 V DC acoustic glass-break detector; normally closed alarm and tamper connections.
identification_notes: Manufacturer photograph of the compact glass-break housing, with its microphone aperture and status indicators.
applicability_limits: This is an acoustic glass-break detector, separate from Impaq shock sensors. The retrieved archive filename mentions INS229-4-2, but the supplied PDF itself prints INS 229-3; check that printed edition against the installed unit.
image_credit: Texecom — official product image

model: Odyssey X wired external sounders — X3 cover shown
protocol: Wired 12 V external sounder/strobe family; SAB/SCB and backlight features depend on the fitted backplate.
identification_notes: Official white-and-blue X3 cover photograph. The manual confirms that several Odyssey X backplates use these covers.
applicability_limits: The outer cover cannot identify Grade 2/3, backlit or wireless electronics. This card lists working wired sounders only; X-W radio and X-D/X-BD dummy deterrents are excluded. Identify the actual backplate before selecting instructions.
image_credit: Texecom — official product image

protocol: Wired DC-powered PIR, with alarm/tamper and masking trouble outputs.
identification_notes: Tall outdoor VXI housing; official picture is the wired version.
applicability_limits: VXI-AM is the wired PIR with anti-masking. VXI-ST lacks anti-masking, VXI-DAM adds microwave, and -R variants are battery/transmitter configurations. Their specifications and wiring differ.
image_credit: Optex — official product image

protocol: Wired 9.5–16 V DC PIR with alarm and tamper outputs.
identification_notes: Smooth two-part outdoor QXI enclosure shown in the exact QXI-ST product page.
applicability_limits: QXI-ST is the wired PIR version. QXI-DT adds microwave; QXI-R/RDT are battery-operated versions intended for a separate transmitter. A shared housing does not establish wireless compatibility.
image_credit: Optex — official product image

protocol: Wired DC-powered PIR with separately configurable left/right alarm outputs.
identification_notes: Official WXI-ST photo of the broad outdoor housing and curved detection window.
applicability_limits: This is wired WXI-ST. Anti-masking WXI-AM and battery-operated WXI-R/RAM have different power, outputs and options; transmitter compatibility must be checked separately.
image_credit: Optex — official product image

protocol: Hardwired DC-powered PIR with alarm/tamper outputs; no radio transmitter in this model.
identification_notes: Slender FTN body with upper/lower window sections, as pictured on the manufacturer FTN-ST page.
applicability_limits: FTN-ST is the standard hardwired model. FTN-AM adds anti-masking; FTN-R/RAM are battery-operated transmitter configurations. The shared datasheet contains all four, so use the FTN-ST column.
image_credit: Optex — official product image

protocol: Wired 9.5–16 V DC PIR with alarm/tamper outputs.
identification_notes: Complete FlipX Standard housing, using the official three-quarter product view rather than the close-up lens image.
applicability_limits: FLX-S-ST is the PIR model. FLX-S-DT adds microwave and has different operating settings. It is separate from FlipX Advanced and Professional families; confirm the label before selecting coverage and wiring.
image_credit: Optex — official product image

protocol: Wired 9.5–16 V DC PIR with normally closed alarm/tamper outputs.
identification_notes: Official RXC product-page photograph. RXC-ST and RXC-DT share this outward style, so the label is necessary.
applicability_limits: The manufacturer lists this product as discontinued. Use the actual RXC-ST label and matching manual edition. RXC-STPL and battery-operated RXC-RST are outside this entry.
image_credit: Optex — official product image

protocol: Wired 9.5–16 V DC PIR plus microwave detector, with alarm/tamper outputs; microwave frequency depends on the exact regional suffix.
identification_notes: Official RXC product-page photograph. RXC-ST and RXC-DT share this outward style, so the label is necessary.
applicability_limits: The manufacturer lists this product as discontinued. Use the actual RXC-DT label and matching manual edition. Do not assume an -X5/-X7/-X8 microwave variant is permitted in the same country; the manual gives a regional table. RXC-RDT is a different battery-operated version.
image_credit: Optex — official product image

protocol: Ajax Jeweller two-way wireless; the saved edition lists 868.0–868.6 or 868.7–869.2 MHz regional versions.
identification_notes: PIR motion detector; rectangular lens below the upper status light.
applicability_limits: MotionProtect Plus adds microwave sensing in a very similar housing. Confirm matching device/hub radio region. The downloadable manual is the dated 2020 edition; current firmware menus and compatibility are in the linked official online guide. Fibra and other similarly named editions are outside this entry.

protocol: Ajax Jeweller two-way wireless; the saved edition lists 868.0–868.6 or 868.7–869.2 MHz regional versions.

applicability_limits: Plus combines PIR with microwave verification; the cover alone does not distinguish it from MotionProtect. Confirm matching device/hub radio region. The downloadable manual is the dated 2020 edition; current firmware menus and compatibility are in the linked official online guide. Fibra and other similarly named editions are outside this entry.
image_credit: Ajax — illustration from the manufacturer manual

protocol: Ajax Jeweller two-way wireless; the saved edition lists 868.0–868.6 or 868.7–869.2 MHz regional versions.
identification_notes: Manufacturer illustration of the motion/glass-break detector with its lens and microphone opening.
applicability_limits: Combines PIR motion and acoustic glass-break detection; it is not a smoke or shock detector. Confirm matching device/hub radio region. The downloadable manual is the dated 2020 edition; current firmware menus and compatibility are in the linked official online guide. Fibra and other similarly named editions are outside this entry.

protocol: Ajax Jeweller two-way wireless; the saved edition lists 868.0–868.6 or 868.7–869.2 MHz regional versions.
identification_notes: Slim opening-detector body and separate magnet, with the mounting plate also shown in the original illustration.
applicability_limits: This is the classic reed-switch opening detector. DoorProtect Plus adds shock and tilt sensing despite a similar appearance. Confirm matching device/hub radio region. The downloadable manual is the dated 2020 edition; current firmware menus and compatibility are in the linked official online guide. Fibra and other similarly named editions are outside this entry.

protocol: Ajax Jeweller two-way wireless; the saved edition lists 868.0–868.6 or 868.7–869.2 MHz regional versions.
identification_notes: Manufacturer illustration of the Plus detector and its magnet; the housing closely resembles DoorProtect.
applicability_limits: Plus provides opening, shock and tilt detection. Identify the model in the label/app; appearance does not prove Plus capability. Confirm matching device/hub radio region. The downloadable manual is the dated 2020 edition; current firmware menus and compatibility are in the linked official online guide. Fibra and other similarly named editions are outside this entry.

protocol: Ajax Jeweller two-way wireless; the saved edition lists 868.0–868.6 or 868.7–869.2 MHz regional versions.
identification_notes: Slim acoustic glass-break housing, shown with its rear mounting plate in the manufacturer illustration.
applicability_limits: This is acoustic glass-break detection, not an opening contact. The microphone and exact label matter more than the similar slim housing. Confirm matching device/hub radio region. The downloadable manual is the dated 2020 edition; current firmware menus and compatibility are in the linked official online guide. Fibra and other similarly named editions are outside this entry.

protocol: Ajax Jeweller two-way wireless; the saved edition lists 868.0–868.6 or 868.7–869.2 MHz regional versions.
identification_notes: Compact square indoor siren with front grille and Ajax nameplate; mounting parts remain visible in the source illustration.
applicability_limits: Indoor siren; it is not the weather-resistant StreetSiren. The external LED connection is not an input for conventional alarm sounder triggering. Confirm matching device/hub radio region. The downloadable manual is the dated 2020 edition; current firmware menus and compatibility are in the linked official online guide. protocol: Ajax Jeweller two-way wireless; the saved edition lists 868.0–868.6 or 868.7–869.2 MHz regional versions.

Fibra and other similarly named editions are outside this entry.

Hub/repeater support in the 2020 manual is historical; check the current online compatibility guide. Confirm matching device/hub radio region. The downloadable manual is the dated 2020 edition; current firmware menus and compatibility are in the linked official online guide. Fibra and other similarly named editions are outside this entry.

protocol: Domestic mains alarm; hardwired interconnect; optional Ei3000MRF SmartLINK module
identification_notes: 3000-series housing marked Heat Alarm, with the heat sensor identified in the Rev4 overview. Check Ei3014 on the label; Ei3016 and Ei3024 use similar shells.
applicability_limits: Aico domestic alarm system. This is not a commercial addressable-loop detector; check the underside model label and whether an RF module is actually fitted.

protocol: Wired 12 V PIR with alarm/tamper outputs and selectable EOL resistance.
identification_notes: Manufacturer IR-100 photograph, with compact lower lens and a single front LED window.
applicability_limits: The 100-series outer style is also used by other models. This entry is wired IR-100, excluding QD-100, IR-100-PET and W-IR-100. Match the IR-100 label and the actual EOL configuration.
image_credit: Orisec — official product image

protocol: Domestic mains alarm; hardwired interconnect; optional Ei3000MRF SmartLINK module
identification_notes: 3000-series optical smoke alarm. The manufacturer picture has Optical Smoke Alarm wording; confirm Ei3016 on the base label.
applicability_limits: Aico domestic alarm system. This is not a commercial addressable-loop detector; check the underside model label and whether an RF module is actually fitted.
image_credit: Aico manufacturer product photograph

protocol: Wired PIR plus microwave detector; alarm/tamper and selectable EOL connections.
identification_notes: Official shared 200-series housing photograph, with the three-part LED area above the lens.
applicability_limits: This entry is DT-200 only. IR/QD, PET, AM, beam and wireless 200-series variants differ internally and cannot be identified by this cover. Confirm microwave region/frequency and label. Manufacturer specifications are linked online; no unverified PDF has been attached.
image_credit: Orisec — official product image

protocol: Domestic mains alarm; hardwired interconnect; optional Ei3000MRF SmartLINK module
identification_notes: 3000-series optical smoke and heat multisensor. Its shared housing does not make it an Ei3014, Ei3016 or Ei3030.
applicability_limits: Aico domestic alarm system. This is not a commercial addressable-loop detector; check the underside model label and whether an RF module is actually fitted. Ei3024 is a fire multisensor, not the Ei3030 fire-and-CO model.
image_credit: Aico manufacturer product photograph

protocol: Orisec two-way wireless with frequency hopping at 868.65 and 869.15 MHz.
identification_notes: Manufacturer family image shows the slim magnetic-contact body and magnet in four finishes; counted as one family.
applicability_limits: This is a magnetic opening contact, not a covert shock detector. The manufacturer page has an inconsistent generic table description, but its title, model heading and product declaration identify W-MC-C as the contact. W-SD-C, W-SD-MC-C, deep backs and waterproof housings are separate products. Check receiver compatibility. Documentation is online only.
image_credit: Orisec — official product image

protocol: Domestic mains alarm; hardwired interconnect; optional Ei3000MRF SmartLINK module
identification_notes: Manufacturer photo carries Multi-Sensor Fire & Carbon Monoxide Alarm wording. The model uses optical, heat and electrochemical CO sensing; check Ei3030 on the label.
applicability_limits: Aico domestic alarm system. This is not a commercial addressable-loop detector; check the underside model label and whether an RF module is actually fitted. The linked B20665 Rev4 is specifically for Ei3030; do not apply the Ei3024 manual as a substitute.
image_credit: Aico manufacturer product photograph

protocol: Wired powered shock-detector family with alarm/tamper and LED-control connections.
identification_notes: Official shared shock-detector photograph presents four finish options for one wired housing family.
applicability_limits: Confirm SD-G2 versus SD-G3 on the label; the grade and sensitivity features differ. This family excludes SD-MC-G2 magnetic-contact, W-SD and covert wireless models. The appearance and finish do not identify the electronics. Manufacturer specifications are online only.
image_credit: Orisec — official product image

protocol: Domestic sealed-battery alarm; RF-upgradable with Ei600MRF
identification_notes: Optical-and-heat alarm in the Ei600 housing. The Rev3 model chart identifies Ei660i as RF-upgradable; Ei660iRF is a separately labelled variant.
applicability_limits: Battery domestic alarm, not a panel-loop head. Confirm the model and fitted module; the picture alone does not prove radio interconnection.
image_credit: Aico manufacturer product photograph

protocol: Wired external sounder/strobe family; conventional or Orisec network wiring as supported by the fitted unit.
